## 28. Vocational Education Reform (职业本科)
**Kategori**: Pendidikan

⏱ Lag: 8-12 tahun — reformasi vokasi sistemik di Indonesia kemungkinan baru terjadi 2030-2035 | 📊 Laggard (tertinggal) — dengan risiko leapfrog jika reformasi radikal dipilih | 🎯 Prob: Tinggi | 🔍 Keyakinan: Sedang

> **Status di Indonesia**: Belum — Indonesia masih jauh tertinggal dalam transformasi sistemik vokasi

### Basic Info

**Tahun Mulai China**: 2019

**Pemain Kunci China**

> Kementerian Pendidikan China (教育部).
> Lembaga: Shenzhen Polytechnic University (深圳职业技术大学), Guangzhou Polytechnic (广州番禺职业技术学院).
> Program: vocational bachelor degree (职业本科).
> Perusahaan mitra: Huawei, BYD, CATL dalam dual-system apprenticeship.

### China Trend Detail

**Apa Yang Terjadi Di China**

> China melakukan reformasi masif sistem pendidikan vokasi 2019-2026: mengubah stigma 'sekolah kejuruan = gagal' menjadi jalur karir bergensi.
> Kebijakan utama: (1) Konversi sekolah vokasi terbaik menjadi universitas sarjana vokasi (职业本科) — menciptakan jalur setara S1 berbasis keterampilan teknis.
> (2) Program upskilling 30 juta pekerja 2025-2027, prioritas IT, CNC/robot, green energy.
> (3) Master profesional ditargetkan 2/3 dari seluruh program master (sebelumnya 50%).
> (4) Dual-system apprenticeship ala Jerman: siswa belajar di kampus + praktik di perusahaan mitra.
> (5) Penghapusan 12.200+ program studi tidak relevan (2021-2025) dan pembukaan 10.200+ prodi baru (AI, robotika, low-altitude, carbon neutrality).
> Konteks: pengangguran fresh graduate tinggi + mismatch skills pasar kerja memaksa reforma sistemik.

**Data Skala China**

> >100 vocational bachelor universities berdiri (Jan 2026, naik dari hanya beberapa).
> Enrollment vokasi sarjana naik 7x lipat (2021-2026).
> Target upskilling: 30 juta pekerja (2025-2027).
> 12.200 program dihapus vs 10.200 dibuka (2021-2025).
> Alokasi anggaran vokasi: target ¥500 miliar/tahun (Rencana Lima Tahun ke-14).
> >8.000 sekolah vokasi tingkat menengah di China (2024).
> Tingkat penempatan kerja lulusan vokasi: >95% dalam 6 bulan (klaim resmi).

**Fase Tren Di China**

> Booming — reformasi masif sedang berjalan, didorong krisis pengangguran fresh graduate dan kebutuhan industri manufaktur lanjutan

**Puncak Tren China**

2025-2030: fase implementasi paling intensif seiring ekspansi robotik dan AI manufaktur

### Status Indonesia Saat Ini

**Status Di Indonesia**: Belum — Indonesia masih jauh tertinggal dalam transformasi sistemik vokasi

**Contoh Konkret Indonesia**

> Politeknik Negeri: masih terbatas dan kurang bergengsi sosial.
> Program SMK: 14.000+ sekolah tapi kualitas tidak merata, banyak peralatan usang.
> Kemendikbud: program Kampus Merdeka ada komponen vokasi tapi belum transformatif.
> Program D4 (Sarjana Terapan) ada tapi enrollment rendah.
> Link-and-match program Kemendikbud dengan industri: baru pilot, belum sistemik.
> Tidak ada padanan '职业本科 university' setara China.

**Data Skala Indonesia**

> Jumlah SMK: >14.000 (terbesar di dunia tapi kualitas rendah).
> Lulusan SMK yang menganggur: 8,49% (2024, tertinggi antar jenjang).
> Politeknik negeri: 45 institusi.
> D4 enrollment: <10% dari total mahasiswa.
> Tingkat kecocokan keterampilan lulusan vokasi dengan industri: rendah (survei APINDO: 60%+ perusahaan keluhkan mismatch).

### Analisis Lag

**Estimasi Lag Tahun**

8-12 tahun — reformasi vokasi sistemik di Indonesia kemungkinan baru terjadi 2030-2035

**Bukti Historical Lag**

> China mulai reformasi vokasi serius 2019; Indonesia baru diskusi 2024-2025.
> Jerman (model dual-system) sudah dicontek China; Indonesia belum.
> Program SMK-DUDI link-and-match sudah dicanangkan >10 tahun lalu tapi implementasi masih parsial.

**Tipe Lag**: Laggard (tertinggal) — dengan risiko leapfrog jika reformasi radikal dipilih

### Probabilitas Transfer ke Indonesia

**Probabilitas Transfer**: Tinggi

**Alasan Probabilitas**

> Tekanan pengangguran sarjana dan mismatch keterampilan di Indonesia identik dengan China.
> Reformasi hampir pasti terjadi — pertanyaannya hanya kecepatan dan kedalamannya.

**Vektor Transmisi**

> Kebijakan pemerintah (Kemendikbud/Kemenperin).
> Studi banding ke China dan Jerman.
> Tekanan industri (Hyundai, BYD, CATL yang masuk Indonesia membutuhkan tenaga teknis terlatih).
> Program beasiswa vokasi China untuk Indonesia.

### Faktor Pendorong

**Prasyarat Struktural**

> Dukungan politik untuk de-stigmatisasi pendidikan vokasi.
> Anggaran pendidikan yang memadai (Indonesia: 20% APBN tapi vokasi dapat porsi kecil).
> Kemitraan industri yang nyata (bukan ceremonial).
> Instruktur berstandar industri.
> Threshold: Indonesia sudah memiliki skala (14.000+ SMK) tapi kualitas dan sistem ekosistem industri belum ada.

**Indikator Pemantauan**

> Pengesahan UU Pendidikan Vokasi (jika ada).
> Anggaran khusus vokasi di APBN.
> Jumlah MoU industri-politeknik yang benar-benar operasional.
> Enrollment D4/Sarjana Terapan vs S1 umum.
> Tingkat penyerapan lulusan vokasi.

### Hambatan & Faktor Pembatal

**Hambatan Transfer**

> Stigma sosial: 'kuliah vokasi = tidak mampu masuk universitas'.
> Orang tua mendorong anak ke S1 umum.
> Kualitas instruktur vokasi rendah (banyak guru SMK tidak punya pengalaman industri).
> Peralatan bengkel/lab usang.
> Kurangnya insentif industri untuk jadi mitra aktif.

**Faktor Pembatal Transfer**

> Reformasi setengah-hati yang hanya ganti nama tanpa ubah substansi.
> Korupsi dalam pengadaan peralatan sekolah vokasi.
> Geografi kepulauan membuat standarisasi sulit.
> Konsentrasi industri di Jawa membuat vokasi daerah sulit mendapat partner industri.

### Prediksi Timeline di Indonesia

**Tahun Masuk Indonesia**

2019-2023: Inisiasi (link-and-match, Kampus Merdeka). 2024-2026: akselerasi terbatas.

**Tahun Mainstream Indonesia**: 2030-2033 (jika ada political will kuat)

**Skenario Percepatan**

> Investasi manufaktur China besar-besaran di Indonesia (BYD, CATL, Xiaomi) memaksa pemerintah melatih tenaga teknis in-situ.
> PHK massal sektor padat karya mendorong retraining masif.

### Dampak Sosial-Ekonomi

**Dampak Lapangan Kerja**

> Positif: teknisi robot/CNC, operator mesin canggih, programmer PLC, teknisi baterai EV, operator drone industri — semua butuh vokasi berstandar tinggi.
> Negatif: pekerja dengan vokasi rendah kualitas makin sulit bersaing.
> Transisi: puluhan ribu instruktur SMK perlu upgrade kompetensi.

**Dampak Kelas Menengah**

> Akses ke vokasi berkualitas bisa jadi elevator sosial baru bagi kelas menengah bawah — alternatif S1 mahal yang tidak menjamin pekerjaan.
> Tapi stigma sosial masih hambatan bagi keluarga kelas menengah yang aspirasi anaknya masuk universitas.

**Dampak Daerah Non Jawa**

> Vokasi bisa lebih relevan di luar Jawa (pertanian presisi, perikanan teknologi, pertambangan modern).
> Tapi tanpa industri mitra di daerah, dual-system apprenticeship tidak bisa jalan.
> Ketimpangan kualitas SMK Jawa vs luar Jawa sangat besar.

### Kaitan Pendidikan

**Jurusan Terancam**

> D3 teknik umum tanpa spesialisasi.
> Guru/instruktur vokasi tidak berstandar industri.
> Program SMK yang tidak link dengan industri nyata.
> Pendidikan umum S1 yang menghasilkan fresh graduate tanpa keterampilan teknis spesifik.

**Jurusan Dibutuhkan**

> Teknik robotika dan otomasi industri.
> Teknik baterai dan energi terbarukan.
> Teknisi kendaraan listrik.
> Operator CNC dan machining presisi.
> Programmer embedded systems dan IoT industri.
> Teknisi drone komersial.
> Manajemen rantai pasok (supply chain) berbasis teknologi.

**China Education Response**

> Pembukaan 职业本科 (vocational bachelor) universities >100 institusi (2026).
> Penghapusan 12.200 prodi tidak relevan.
> Prodi baru: 低空技术与工程 (Low-Altitude Tech), 智能机器人 (Intelligent Robotics), 碳中和 (Carbon Neutrality), 新能源汽车 (New Energy Vehicles).
> Sistem '1+X' sertifikasi: siswa dapat sertifikasi industri tambahan di luar ijazah.
> Dual-system dengan Huawei, CATL, BYD sebagai mitra wajib.

### Pelajaran Kebijakan dari China

**Respons Kebijakan China**

> UU Vokasi 2022 (Vocational Education Law revisi): setarakan pendidikan vokasi dengan akademik secara hukum.
> Larangan universitas umum merendahkan lulusan vokasi dalam rekrutmen.
> Subsidi perusahaan mitra apprenticeship.
> Rekrutmen PNS tidak boleh diskriminasi latar vokasi.
> Sertifikasi instruktur: wajib pengalaman industri 2 tahun sebelum mengajar.

**Rekomendasi Kebijakan Indonesia**

> 1) UU Pendidikan Vokasi yang setarakan D4/sarjana terapan dengan S1.
> 2) Insentif pajak bagi perusahaan yang jadi mitra apprenticeship aktif.
> 3) Larangan diskriminasi rekrutmen berbasis jalur pendidikan (vokasi vs akademik).
> 4) Standarisasi kompetensi instruktur SMK/politeknik dengan pengalaman industri wajib.
> 5) Dana BOS Vokasi khusus untuk pengadaan peralatan berstandar industri.

### Peluang & Rekomendasi Aksi

**Peluang Bisnis**

> Lembaga pelatihan/kursus vokasi berstandar industri (coding, CNC, robotika).
> Vendor peralatan bengkel SMK (pasar besar jika ada program modernisasi).
> Platform e-learning vokasi berbahasa Indonesia.
> Konsultasi kurikulum vokasi untuk Kemendikbud.
> Jasa sertifikasi kompetensi industri.

**Rekomendasi Individu Mahasiswa**

> Ambil sertifikasi teknis industri di luar gelar formal (Google, AWS, Huawei certification).
> Cari program magang di industri manufaktur lanjutan.
> Kuasai bahasa Mandarin — banyak instruktur teknis dari perusahaan China.
> Jangan remehkan D4/Politeknik jika spesialisasinya relevan dengan industri.

**Rekomendasi Perguruan Tinggi**

> Politeknik: transform ke dual-system dengan industri nyata, bukan MoU seremonial.
> Buka program Teknik Robotika, Teknisi EV, Energi Terbarukan.
> Rekrut instruktur dari industri (bukan hanya akademisi).
> Universitas umum: buka minor vokasi teknis untuk mahasiswa S1 non-teknik.

### Faktor Risiko & Sisi Gelap

**Dampak Negatif China**

> Stigma sosial yang sulit hilang: keluarga tetap mendorong anak ke universitas umum meski susah dapat kerja.
> Kesenjangan kualitas antara vokasi kota tier-1 vs daerah pedalaman.
> Komersialisasi sertifikasi '1+X' — banyak sertifikat yang tidak diakui industri nyata.
> Overpromise: tingkat penempatan kerja yang diklaim tinggi tidak selalu mencerminkan kualitas pekerjaan.

**Risiko Sosial Indonesia**

> Reformasi setengah-hati menciptakan lulusan vokasi yang tetap tidak terserap industri.
> Investasi keluarga miskin di SMK/politeknik berakhir sia-sia jika link industri tidak nyata.
> Konsentrasi industri di Jawa membuat lulusan vokasi luar Jawa harus migrasi atau menganggur.

**Unintended Consequences**

> Kompetisi sertifikasi yang tidak terstandar dapat menciptakan 'sertifikat sampah'.
> Ekspansi vokasi tanpa instruktur berkualitas menurunkan standar keseluruhan.
> Dual-system bisa jadi eksploitasi tenaga magang murah oleh perusahaan.

**Kelompok Rentan**

> Siswa SMK dari keluarga miskin yang tidak bisa memilih sekolah vokasi berkualitas.
> Lulusan SMK jurusan tidak relevan (tata busana, teknik lama) yang tidak ter-upgrade.
> Instruktur SMK lama yang tidak punya keterampilan industri terkini.

### Contoh Kasus Konkret

**Kasus China**

> Shenzhen Polytechnic University (深圳职业技术大学): upgraded menjadi universitas penuh 2023, kini benchmark vokasi modern China.
> Program CATL-Vocational: >20 sekolah vokasi menjadi mitra resmi pabrik baterai terbesar dunia.
> Revolusi '1+X': >500 jenis sertifikasi industri terintegrasi ke kurikulum vokasi.
> Tencent, Alibaba membuka 'vocational college' digital sendiri.

**Padanan Indonesia**

> Politeknik Elektronika Negeri Surabaya (PENS): benchmark politeknik Indonesia tapi masih jauh dari standar China.
> SMK-DUDI Program Kemendikbud: sudah jalan tapi MoU lebih banyak di atas kertas.
> Program vokasi LPDP: baru mulai.
> Huawei ICT Academy: model kemitraan industri yang cukup nyata di Indonesia.

**Sumber Data Kunci**

> Kemendikbud Statistik Pendidikan Vokasi.
> 教育部 China Ministry of Education annual reports.
> World Bank Indonesia vocational education assessment 2023.
> APINDO survey mismatch keterampilan.

### Tingkat Keyakinan & Kualitas Sumber

**Catatan Kontradiksi Data**

> Data tingkat penempatan kerja vokasi China sangat optimistis dari sumber resmi; sumber independen menunjukkan realitas lebih kompleks.
> Data Indonesia untuk vokasi tersebar di berbagai kementerian (Kemendikbud, Kemenperin, Kemenaker) dan tidak terintegrasi.

### ⚠️ Field Tidak Pasti

- `tahun_puncak_indonesia`
- `data_skala_china enrollment vokasi sarjana 7x`

## 29. 'AI+' National Policy & Mass AI Diffusion — the state-orchestrated, target-driven diffusion of AI into every sector of the economy and society (as distinct from AI research/model-building policy), measured by binding penetration targets, sectoral action plans, compute subsidies, and population-scale consumer adoption
**Kategori**: Regulasi & Kebijakan (Regulation & Policy) — specifically industrial/diffusion policy and digital-governance architecture, with heavy spillovers into Digital Economy, Public Administration, Education Policy, and Labor Policy

📊 LAGGARD on state-driven diffusion policy (5-7 years, and structurally so — Indonesia lacks the target-cascade machinery, not merely the timing), NEAR-SIMULTANEOUS on consumer AI usage (~2 years and compressing), and with a genuine LEAPFROG OPTION on capability: because China open-weights its frontier models (DeepSeek, Qwen), Indonesia can obtain in 2026 the model capability China spent tens of billions building, at effectively zero licence cost. The realistic risk is a THIRD pattern — 'adoption without absorption': Indonesian society consumes foreign AI at near-Chinese rates while the Indonesian state neither directs the diffusion, captures the value, nor regulates the harms. | 🎯 Prob: MASS AI DIFFUSION ITSELF: TINGGI (HIGH) — already happening, market-led. THE CHINESE POLICY MODEL (numeric penetration targets + sectoral action plans + demand-side compute/model vouchers + SOE mandates): RENDAH-SEDANG (LOW-MEDIUM). Selective policy borrowing (AI content labelling, risk tiering, government-adoption roadmaps, sovereign AI fund, WAICO alignment): SEDANG-TINGGI (MEDIUM-HIGH). | 🔍 Keyakinan: TINGGI untuk fakta kebijakan; SEDANG untuk data adopsi; RENDAH untuk proyeksi (HIGH on policy facts; MEDIUM on adoption data; LOW on projections). HIGH confidence: the State Council AI+ Opinions and their 70%/2027, 90%/2030, 2035 targets and six domains (multiply corroborated by gov.cn, CSET translation, MERICS, Global Times, Lawfare); the 2026 sectoral action plans (MIIT AI+ Manufacturing, MOFCOM AI+ Consumption 18 Jun 2026, MOE AI+ Education 10 Apr 2026); the AI companion Interim Measures (issued 10 Apr 2026, effective 15 Jul 2026) and the resulting Doubao/Qwen shutdowns; QuestMobile MAU figures for Aug 2025 (Doubao 157m, DeepSeek 143m) and May 2026 (499m total; 382m/167m/130m); CNNIC 57th report figures (602m generative-AI users, 42.8%, +141.7% YoY); China's core AI industry at >1.2 trillion yuan in 2025 (+40%); APJII 2026 Indonesian figures (81.72% penetration, 235.26m users, 18.2% AI usage); the unsigned status of Indonesia's two AI Perpres as of August 2026; Indonesia's WAICO founding membership (17 Jul 2026); Permendikdasmen 13/2025 making Coding and AI optional. MEDIUM confidence: China's enterprise adoption percentages (survey-based, definitions inconsistent); the 1.4 trillion tokens/day figure (single official source, methodology undisclosed, and vulnerable to metric-gaming once it became a governed KPI); Indonesian organizational AI implementation (~23-26%); Indonesian AI investment totals; the derived ~14.9% Indonesian population penetration (arithmetic on APJII's survey base, not a published statistic). LOW confidence: all economic projections (12%/US$366bn GDP by 2030; 3.67% GDP uplift; US$10.9bn market by 2030 — different methodologies, not reconcilable); all Indonesian timeline predictions in this record; the claim that China will actually reach 70% penetration by 2027 (the term 'penetration of new-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents' is not operationally defined in the public text, so the target may be unfalsifiable by design).

> **Status di Indonesia**: BELUM ADA PADANAN KEBIJAKAN (NO EQUIVALENT POLICY YET) — the sharpest institutional gap in this entire research series. Indonesia has strategy documents but no diffusion mandate: no numeric penetration target, no sectoral action plans, no compute or model vouchers, no dedicated budget line, and — as of August 2026 — not even a signed Presidential Regulation. The two draft Perpres (National AI Roadmap and AI Ethics/Governance) have slipped at least three announced deadlines (early 2026 → H1 2026 → still awaiting the President's signature). On the CONSUMER side, however, Indonesia is not absent: roughly 42-43 million Indonesians have used generative AI, and Indonesia is a top-15 ChatGPT market globally. The pattern is therefore MARKET-LED DIFFUSION WITHOUT STATE ORCHESTRATION — the mirror image of China.

### Basic Info

**Pemain Kunci China**

> STATE / POLICY ACTORS: State Council (issuer of the 'AI+' Opinions, 26-27 Aug 2025, and owner of the 70%/90%/2035 targets); National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC — lead coordinator, 'AI+' scenario lists); Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT — 'AI+ Manufacturing' special action with eight other agencies; >50 national and industry AI standards targeted by 2026); Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM — 'AI+ Consumption' opinions, 18 June 2026, with seven other departments); Ministry of Education (MOE — 'AI+ Education' action plan, 10 April 2026, full system build-out by 2030); Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC — the governance counterweight: generative-AI interim measures 2023, AI content-labelling measures effective 1 Sept 2025, AI anthropomorphic-interaction/companion measures issued 10 April 2026 effective 15 July 2026); National Data Bureau (Liu Liehong — publishes national token-consumption metrics as a diffusion KPI); SASAC and central SOEs (mandated early adopters); provincial and municipal governments (Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, Guangdong — compute vouchers 算力券, model vouchers 模型券, corpus subsidies).

MODEL / PLATFORM COMPANIES: ByteDance (Doubao — the single largest diffusion vehicle, 157m MAU Aug 2025 rising to 382m by May 2026, and >1.2 trillion tokens/day by April 2026); DeepSeek (open-weight R1/V3 — the cost collapse that made mass diffusion economically possible; 143m MAU Aug 2025); Alibaba (Qwen/Tongyi — 167m MAU May 2026, largest open-weight derivative ecosystem globally; Alibaba Cloud as the export arm into Southeast Asia); Tencent (Yuanbao, Hunyuan, enterprise AI); Moonshot (Kimi), Zhipu AI, MiniMax, StepFun, Baidu (Ernie), iFlytek (education/healthcare verticals), Huawei (Ascend compute + Pangu industrial models — the state-preferred full-stack vendor).

DIFFUSION INFRASTRUCTURE: national integrated computing network ('East Data West Computing'); intelligent computing centres (1.59 million PFLOPS installed by end-2025); QuestMobile and CNNIC (the measurement apparatus that makes penetration legible and therefore governable); the 1 trillion RMB state venture capital fund for AI, robotics and frontier tech under the 15th Five-Year Plan.

### China Trend Detail

**Apa Yang Terjadi Di China**

> China has converted AI from an innovation policy into a DIFFUSION policy — and in doing so has become the first country to set quantified, government-owned adoption targets for a general-purpose technology across the whole economy.
> Five mechanisms make it work.

(1) A TARGET ARCHITECTURE, NOT A VISION STATEMENT.
> The State Council's 'AI+' Opinions (26-27 Aug 2025) is deliberately modelled on 'Internet+' (2015), but where 'Internet+' was directional, 'AI+' is numeric: penetration of next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents to exceed 70% by 2027 and 90% by 2030, with AI becoming a principal driver of growth by 2030 and a 'fully intelligent economy and society' by 2035.
> Six domains are named — science and technology, industrial development, consumption, people's wellbeing/public welfare, governance, and global cooperation.
> Because the targets are numeric and dated, they can be cascaded to ministries, provinces and SOEs as performance indicators, which is the entire point: in the Chinese system, what is measured and assigned is what gets built.

(2) CASCADE INTO SECTORAL ACTION PLANS.
> The umbrella document is deliberately thin; the operative content arrives in ministry-level implementation plans issued through 2026.
> MIIT and eight agencies run the 'AI+ Manufacturing' special action to 2027 with concrete deliverables — 3 to 5 general-purpose industrial foundation models, 1,000 industrial intelligent agents, 100 high-quality manufacturing datasets, 500 demonstration scenarios.
> MOFCOM and seven departments issued 'AI+ Consumption' implementation opinions (18 June 2026) covering retail, tourism, hospitality and services.
> MOE issued an 'AI+ Education' action plan (10 April 2026) building an AI education system from primary school to university with full implementation by 2030.
> NDRC maintains lists of 'strategic high-value scenarios' (reported at around 40) that direct where deployment effort goes.
> MIIT targets more than 50 national and industry AI standards by 2026 — standards being the quiet instrument that makes enterprise procurement safe and therefore fast.

(3) SUBSIDISED DEMAND, NOT JUST SUBSIDISED SUPPLY.
> This is the most copyable innovation.
> Provinces issue compute vouchers (算力券), model vouchers (模型券) and corpus/data subsidies that pay firms to CONSUME AI rather than only paying labs to build it.
> Shanghai alone committed roughly 900 million CNY for access to computing clusters, models and training data plus around 500 million CNY over three to five years for enterprise innovation.
> Because the binding constraint on diffusion is buyer-side cost and risk, not seller-side capability, demand subsidies move penetration faster than R&D grants.

(4) A CONSUMER FLYWHEEL RUNNING AHEAD OF THE POLICY.
> Mass adoption was not created by the plan — it was already happening and the plan rides it.
> CNNIC's 57th report (5 Feb 2026) puts generative-AI users at 602 million, 42.8% of the population, up 141.7% year-on-year from 249 million (17.6%) at end-2024.
> China's AI-native apps reached 499 million MAU by May 2026, +85.4% YoY, with users averaging 92.7 sessions and 183 minutes per month.
> Daily national token consumption rose from about 100 billion in early 2024 to 1.4 trillion by March 2026 — more than a thousandfold in two years — a metric the National Data Bureau now publishes precisely because it is the cleanest available proxy for diffusion.
> Free-to-user pricing (Doubao, DeepSeek, Qwen all free at the consumer tier) is itself an implicit subsidy that no other market has matched at this scale.

(5) GOVERNANCE APPLIED TO HARMS, NOT TO ADOPTION.
> Uniquely, China is simultaneously the world's most aggressive AI-adoption promoter AND one of its most prescriptive AI regulators — but the regulation targets specific harms rather than the diffusion itself.
> AI-generated content labelling became mandatory on 1 September 2025.
> The Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services (issued 10 April 2026 by CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR; effective 15 July 2026) banned virtual-companion and virtual-family services for minors, required guardian consent for users under 14, and imposed anti-addiction and safety-assessment duties — forcing ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen to shut down personalised companion agents used by very large user bases.
> Notably, the same interim measures explicitly EXEMPT customer service, Q&A, work assistants, education and research — i.e.
> the regulator carved out exactly the productivity uses the AI+ plan is trying to scale.
> The AI+ Opinions themselves instruct officials to 'strengthen employment risk assessments for AI applications' and to steer innovation resources toward job-creating directions, and an 'AI + Employment' framework (tax incentives, reskilling, wage subsidies) is under discussion.

The net effect is a state that treats AI penetration as infrastructure policy — comparable to electrification or highway build-out — with quantified coverage targets, subsidised uptake, standardised interfaces, sectoral rollout plans, and a separate harm-specific regulatory track that does not slow the rollout.

**Fase Tren Di China**

> BOOMING and STATE-ACCELERATED, entering the mid-phase of a policy cycle that is unusual for running adoption and harm-regulation on parallel tracks.
> Sequence: policy formation (Mar 2024 'AI+' named in the Government Work Report) → mandate issued (Aug 2025 State Council Opinions with numeric targets) → operationalisation and cascade (2026: 15th Five-Year Plan absorption, MOE/MOFCOM/MIIT sectoral plans, provincial voucher schemes, standards build-out) → the 2027 checkpoint (70% target) → saturation target 2030 (90%) → declared endpoint 2035.
> Consumer adoption is in explosive growth (42.8% population penetration, +141.7% YoY) and shows no plateau.
> Simultaneously the harm-regulation track is already in ENFORCEMENT phase — content labelling live since Sept 2025 and companion-AI restrictions live since July 2026 with real product shutdowns — which is remarkable: China is regulating specific AI harms while its penetration curve is still steepening, rather than after saturation as it did with platforms (2020-2022) and fintech.
> There is no backlash phase against diffusion itself; the visible backlash is narrow and targeted (minors, emotional dependence, deepfakes, employment displacement).

### Status Indonesia Saat Ini

**Status Di Indonesia**

> BELUM ADA PADANAN KEBIJAKAN (NO EQUIVALENT POLICY YET) — the sharpest institutional gap in this entire research series.
> Indonesia has strategy documents but no diffusion mandate: no numeric penetration target, no sectoral action plans, no compute or model vouchers, no dedicated budget line, and — as of August 2026 — not even a signed Presidential Regulation.
> The two draft Perpres (National AI Roadmap and AI Ethics/Governance) have slipped at least three announced deadlines (early 2026 → H1 2026 → still awaiting the President's signature).
> On the CONSUMER side, however, Indonesia is not absent: roughly 42-43 million Indonesians have used generative AI, and Indonesia is a top-15 ChatGPT market globally.
> The pattern is therefore MARKET-LED DIFFUSION WITHOUT STATE ORCHESTRATION — the mirror image of China.

**Contoh Konkret Indonesia**

> STRATEGY DOCUMENTS (non-binding).
> Strategi Nasional Kecerdasan Artifisial (Stranas KA) 2020-2045, launched August 2020 — four focus areas (ethics/policy, talent, infrastructure/data, industrial research) and five priority sectors (health, bureaucratic reform, education and research, food security, mobility/smart cities), but no enforceable standards, no dedicated implementing agency, and no monitoring mechanism.
> Komdigi Circular Letter (Surat Edaran) No.
> 9/2023 on AI ethics — voluntary, unenforceable.

THE PENDING PERPRES.
> Komdigi's National AI Roadmap White Paper (179 pages, public consultation from August 2025) and two draft Presidential Regulations: (a) National AI Roadmap (variously reported as 2026-2029 and 2026-2030) and (b) AI Ethics/Governance with a three-tier risk classification and harm-mitigation duties.
> Contents reported from the drafts: government bodies to adopt AI progressively across 2026-2029; AI projected to add up to 12% to GDP (~US$366 billion) by 2030; mandatory reporting of AI-related risks including biometric misuse, IP violation and deepfakes; AI-generated content labelling/watermarking as the FIRST implementing regulation; a 'Sovereign AI Fund' to be established 2027-2029 and managed primarily by Danantara (the sovereign wealth manager overseeing >US$900bn in state assets) using blended public-private finance for fundamental research, public-sector pilots, and data/compute infrastructure.
> As of August 2026 neither Perpres has been signed; Komdigi has said both cleared harmonisation and sit at the State Secretariat.

EIGHT 'QUICK WIN' PROJECTS (from the white paper): AI monitoring of the Makan Bergizi Gratis free nutritious-meal programme (~US$15bn, 83 million beneficiaries — attendance tracking and meal distribution), crop-yield forecasting for food self-sufficiency, and financial-report tracking inside the Koperasi Desa Merah Putih programme, among others.

GOVTECH.
> INA Digital / GovTech national rollout scheduled for October 2026 under President Prabowo, AI-supported, with roughly 80% of the system already connected and AI-processed data integration implemented across eight ministries and agencies.

SOVEREIGN CAPABILITY.
> Sahabat-AI — Indonesia's open-source LLM built by Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison with GoTo and Nvidia support, covering Bahasa Indonesia and regional languages, released as a consumer app on Android and iOS in February 2026 and endorsed by Komdigi as aligned with the national roadmap.
> AI Center of Excellence with Indosat, Nvidia and Cisco (target: 1 million Indonesians with digital/AI skills by 2027).
> Komdigi's AI Talent Factory under the Digital Talent Development Centre.
> BDx Indonesia's sovereign AI data centre (Dec 2024) and Indosat's AI Factory — the first in Southeast Asia to integrate Nvidia GB200 NVL72 systems.

EDUCATION.
> Permendikdasmen No.
> 13/2025 made Coding and Artificial Intelligence an OPTIONAL subject from the 2025/2026 school year, phased in at grade 5 (SD), grade 7 (SMP) and grade 10 (SMA/SMK); explicitly not compulsory for schools lacking facilities.
> Teacher self-paced coding/AI training participation reported at 97% by July 2026; ImajiNation 2026 competition targeting 11,000+ participants from 2,000 schools across 38 provinces.

CHINA VECTOR.
> Indonesia became a FOUNDING MEMBER of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO) in Shanghai on 17 July 2026, alongside 28 other economies, signed by Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto — the single clearest signal of policy alignment with the Chinese AI-governance bloc.
> Chinese counterparts engaged: ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent, Huawei, Deep Robotics, Unitree, FiberHome.
> Tencent has introduced enterprise AI products to J&T Express, Traveloka and GDP Venture; a Joint Laboratory for Digital Medicine and Proactive Health has been established; a Tsinghua University AI-focused branch campus has been proposed; AIonOS and Indosat are building DeepSeek-powered solutions for tourism, knowledge economy and sustainable agriculture.

### Analisis Lag

**Bukti Historical Lag**

> (1) THE 'INTERNET+' PRECEDENT IS THE CLEANEST ANALOGUE.
> China wrote 'Internet+' into the Government Work Report in March 2015 with a cascade of ministerial implementation plans; Indonesia's comparable framing — Making Indonesia 4.0 (2018) and the Peta Jalan Indonesia Digital 2021-2024 — arrived 3-6 years later and, critically, without numeric adoption targets or demand subsidies.
> The same structural difference is repeating with AI+, which suggests the gap is institutional rather than temporal.
(2) AI STRATEGY ITSELF.
> China's New Generation AI Development Plan: July 2017.
> Indonesia's Stranas KA: August 2020 — a 3-year lag on the strategy document, but Stranas KA has produced no binding regulation in six years, so the effective lag on IMPLEMENTED policy is much larger than three years.
(3) DATA-PROTECTION LAW AS A CALIBRATION POINT.
> China's PIPL took effect November 2021; Indonesia's UU PDP was passed in 2022 with a two-year transition to October 2024 and an implementing regulation and supervisory authority still incomplete well into 2026.
> Indonesia can pass headline laws close to China's timing but consistently lags by years on implementing regulations, institutions and enforcement — exactly the failure mode now visible with the AI Perpres.
(4) CONSUMER TECHNOLOGY LAGS HAVE BEEN COMPRESSING.
> Livestream/social commerce: China 2019-2021, Indonesia 2021-2023 (2-3 yrs).
> QR payments: China 2015-2017, Indonesia (QRIS) 2019-2023 (4-6 yrs).
> Ride-hailing/gig platforms: ~2 yrs.
> Generative AI consumer adoption at ~2 yrs is the shortest yet, consistent with the rule that software delivered over the internet transfers fastest and capital-intensive or institution-intensive things transfer slowest.
(5) THE ASYMMETRY THAT DEFINES THIS ITEM.
> Every prior trend showed Indonesia's lag closing on the USAGE side while remaining wide on the POLICY side (gig-worker protection, platform regulation, fintech supervision all arrived years after the phenomenon).
> AI+ is the same pattern in a more consequential form: adoption is arriving before the state has any instrument to direct, subsidise, measure or restrain it.

**Tipe Lag**

> LAGGARD on state-driven diffusion policy (5-7 years, and structurally so — Indonesia lacks the target-cascade machinery, not merely the timing), NEAR-SIMULTANEOUS on consumer AI usage (~2 years and compressing), and with a genuine LEAPFROG OPTION on capability: because China open-weights its frontier models (DeepSeek, Qwen), Indonesia can obtain in 2026 the model capability China spent tens of billions building, at effectively zero licence cost.
> The realistic risk is a THIRD pattern — 'adoption without absorption': Indonesian society consumes foreign AI at near-Chinese rates while the Indonesian state neither directs the diffusion, captures the value, nor regulates the harms.

### Probabilitas Transfer ke Indonesia

**Probabilitas Transfer**

> MASS AI DIFFUSION ITSELF: TINGGI (HIGH) — already happening, market-led.
> THE CHINESE POLICY MODEL (numeric penetration targets + sectoral action plans + demand-side compute/model vouchers + SOE mandates): RENDAH-SEDANG (LOW-MEDIUM).
> Selective policy borrowing (AI content labelling, risk tiering, government-adoption roadmaps, sovereign AI fund, WAICO alignment): SEDANG-TINGGI (MEDIUM-HIGH).

**Alasan Probabilitas**

> WHY THE TECHNOLOGY TRANSFERS EASILY (high probability): (a) Delivery is software over the internet at zero marginal cost, into a country with 81.72% internet penetration — higher than China's.
> (b) The leading Chinese models are OPEN WEIGHT: DeepSeek and Qwen can be downloaded and deployed by any Indonesian firm without permission, price negotiation or export licence; Qwen has the largest open-weight derivative ecosystem on Hugging Face.
> (c) Chinese vendors are actively selling into Indonesia — Alibaba Cloud, Huawei, Tencent (J&T Express, Traveloka, GDP Venture), with Indosat/AIonOS building DeepSeek-based products.
> (d) Consumer demand is self-propelling: Indonesia is already a top-15 ChatGPT market and Gen Z adoption is rising fast without any policy push.

WHY THE CHINESE POLICY MODEL LARGELY DOES NOT TRANSFER (low-medium probability): (i) NO TARGET-CASCADE MACHINERY.
> China's 70%/90% works because targets can be assigned to ministries, provinces, SASAC and SOEs as evaluated performance indicators.
> Indonesia's state has no comparable instrument for the private sector; the closest analogues (TKDN local-content rules, BUMN directives) apply to procurement and ownership, not technology adoption rates, and Indonesia's post-decentralisation centre-region relationship cannot compel 38 provinces and 500+ regencies onto a common adoption schedule.
> (ii) NO FISCAL ROOM FOR DEMAND SUBSIDIES.
> Shanghai alone committed roughly 1.4 billion CNY in municipal AI subsidies; Indonesia's fiscal space in 2026 is dominated by the ~US$15bn free-meals programme, and the proposed Sovereign AI Fund is deferred to 2027-2029 with no committed amount.
> (iii) NO STATE-OWNED ADOPTION VANGUARD OF EQUIVALENT WEIGHT.
> China's central SOEs are directed early adopters across heavy industry; Indonesia's BUMN are fewer, more fiscally constrained, and being restructured under Danantara rather than tasked with technology diffusion.
> (iv) IMPLEMENTATION CAPACITY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, NOT INTENT.
> The AI Perpres has missed three announced deadlines; Stranas KA produced nothing binding in six years; UU PDP's supervisory authority remains incomplete.
> A document that cannot be signed cannot cascade.
> (v) NO COMPUTE OR TALENT BASE TO ABSORB A MANDATE.
> 580 MW of data-centre capacity and a 400,000-500,000/year talent shortfall mean a 70%-style target would be unmeetable and therefore not credibly set.

WHY SELECTIVE BORROWING IS LIKELY (medium-high): Indonesia has already joined WAICO as a founding member (17 July 2026), imports governance concepts readily (risk tiering echoes both the EU AI Act and Chinese practice; AI content labelling as the first implementing rule directly parallels China's Sept 2025 measures), and has an explicit government-adoption roadmap for 2026-2029 plus a sovereign fund concept that mirrors Chinese state-capital practice.
> The likely outcome is Chinese-STYLE governance instruments without Chinese-SCALE diffusion instruments.

**Vektor Transmisi**

> (a) OPEN-WEIGHT MODEL DIFFUSION — the dominant and most under-appreciated vector.
> DeepSeek and Qwen are released under permissive licences; Indonesian firms, universities and government agencies can download and self-host frontier-adjacent capability with no commercial relationship, no data-residency problem, and no procurement process.
> Indosat/AIonOS is already building DeepSeek-based solutions for tourism, knowledge economy and agriculture.
> This vector requires no Chinese company to enter Indonesia at all, which makes it both the fastest and the least politically visible route.

(b) DIRECT ENTRY BY CHINESE PLATFORM AND CLOUD VENDORS — Alibaba Cloud (Qwen, Wan video models, multi-city AI talent roadshows, Telkom AI Centre of Excellence partnership), Huawei (partner ecosystem, Ascend compute, Pangu industrial models), Tencent (enterprise AI already deployed at J&T Express, Traveloka, GDP Venture), ByteDance (Tokopedia, plus Doubao's product playbook), Deep Robotics, Unitree and FiberHome.
> These firms bring not just products but the CHINESE DEPLOYMENT PLAYBOOK — free consumer tier, aggressive vertical agents, subsidised onboarding.

(c) STATE-TO-STATE POLICY DIFFUSION — the newest and most important vector for this specific item.
> Indonesia's founding membership of the World AI Cooperation Organization (Shanghai, 17 July 2026), signed by the Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, places Indonesia inside a China-anchored AI governance bloc.
> Expect the transmission of standards, model-evaluation frameworks, governance templates, capacity-building programmes, and the conceptual vocabulary of 'AI+' sectoral action plans through this channel, plus bilateral vehicles such as the Joint Laboratory for Digital Medicine and Proactive Health.

(d) EDUCATIONAL AND TALENT CHANNELS — a proposed Tsinghua University AI branch campus in Indonesia; Alibaba Cloud and Huawei certification pipelines; Indonesian graduates of Chinese universities returning with Chinese-style deployment practice; the Komdigi AI Talent Factory and the Indosat/Nvidia/Cisco AI Centre of Excellence as competing Western-aligned pipelines.

(e) LOCAL COPYCAT AND ADAPTATION — Sahabat-AI is functionally an Indonesian answer to the Chinese sovereign-model logic (national LLM, local languages, open source, state endorsement, telco-backed); Indonesian SaaS vendors are packaging foreign models into WhatsApp-native vertical agents at UMKM price points.

(f) INFRASTRUCTURE AND CAPITAL — Chinese and Chinese-linked data-centre, cloud and GPU investment lowers local inference cost and quietly determines which model families become default.

(g) ALGORITHMIC CONTENT DIFFUSION — TikTok/Douyin-origin AI-usage norms, AI video and companion-app formats, and 'AI+' framing spreading through Indonesian social media well ahead of any policy.

WHAT IS NOT TRANSFERRING: the enforcement stack — target cascades to subnational governments, SOE adoption mandates, compute vouchers, mandatory standards, and a measurement apparatus (CNNIC/QuestMobile/National Data Bureau token metrics) that makes penetration legible enough to govern.

### Faktor Pendorong

**Prasyarat Struktural**

> CONDITIONS REQUIRED FOR A CHINA-STYLE NATIONAL AI DIFFUSION PROGRAMME, AND INDONESIA'S POSITION ON EACH:

1) CONNECTIVITY BASE — threshold ~75-80% internet penetration.
> China at AI+ launch (2025): ~80%, 1.125 billion netizens.
> Indonesia (2026): 81.72%, 235.3 million users.
> STATUS: MET AND EXCEEDED.
> Connectivity is emphatically not the constraint.

2) A FREE, LOCALLY-TUNED, MASS-MARKET ASSISTANT.
> China's consumer surge rests on free apps with excellent Mandarin performance (Doubao 382m MAU, Qwen 167m, DeepSeek 130m by May 2026).
> Indonesia has Sahabat-AI (open source, Indonesian + regional languages, app released Feb 2026) but nothing at Doubao's distribution scale; most Indonesian usage is ChatGPT in a second language.
> STATUS: PARTIALLY MET — this is the single biggest lever on the consumer penetration gap (14.9% vs 42.8%).

3) INCOME AND WILLINGNESS TO PAY / SUBSIDISE.
> China's GDP per capita ~US$13,900 versus Indonesia's ~US$5,400 (about 39%).
> At consumer level this matters less than expected because the leading Chinese apps are free; at ENTERPRISE level it is decisive, because integration, tuning and governance costs are dollar-denominated while Indonesian wages are not.
> STATUS: NOT MET at enterprise scale.

4) COMPUTE CAPACITY.
> China: 1.59 million PFLOPS of intelligent compute (end-2025), >35% of total computing capacity intelligent in 2026, and 1.4 trillion tokens/day of actual consumption.
> Indonesia: ~580 MW of data-centre capacity, +1.3 GW sought, one sovereign AI data centre and one GB200-class AI factory.
> STATUS: NOT MET — and grid reliability and power cost outside Java-Bali cap what can be built.

5) STATE CAPACITY TO SET AND CASCADE TARGETS.
> Requires (a) an accountable subnational hierarchy, (b) evaluated performance indicators, (c) an adoption-mandated state enterprise sector, (d) a measurement apparatus.
> China has all four.
> Indonesia has none in usable form: decentralised regional government, no adoption KPIs, BUMN under restructuring, and no national AI-usage statistic beyond an annual APJII survey question.
> STATUS: NOT MET — and this is a structural feature of Indonesia's political system, not a fixable gap.

6) FISCAL INSTRUMENT FOR DEMAND SUBSIDY.
> China: provincial compute and model vouchers, 1 trillion RMB state VC fund, Shanghai's ~1.4 billion CNY.
> Indonesia: Sovereign AI Fund proposed for 2027-2029, unfunded, with fiscal space consumed by the free-meals programme.
> STATUS: NOT MET.

7) A SIGNED, ENFORCEABLE LEGAL BASIS.
> Minimum viable: a Presidential Regulation with sanctions, an implementing-agency assignment, and derivative ministerial rules.
> Indonesia has drafts pending since 2025 with three missed deadlines and reporting that the framework will be guidance-oriented rather than sanction-backed.
> STATUS: NOT MET — this is the immediate blocker.

8) TALENT TO OPERATE.
> China: >6,600 AI companies, a deep engineering base.
> Indonesia: 9 million digital talents needed by 2030 against 100,000-200,000 produced per year.
> STATUS: SEVERELY UNMET.

9) DATA AND LANGUAGE INFRASTRUCTURE.
> Public corpora for Bahasa Indonesia and 700+ regional languages, plus digitised sectoral data (health, tax, legal, agriculture) that agents can actually act on.
> STATUS: EARLY — Sahabat-AI is the main effort; most government data remains un-digitised or siloed, which caps the value of any adoption target.

10) MEASUREMENT.
> You cannot manage a penetration target you cannot measure.
> China publishes generative-AI user counts (CNNIC), app MAU (QuestMobile) and daily national token consumption (National Data Bureau).
> Indonesia's only recurring national AI-usage figure is a single APJII survey question.
> STATUS: NOT MET — and it is the cheapest of all these gaps to close.

**Indikator Pemantauan**

> SIGNALS THAT INDONESIA IS MOVING TOWARD A REAL DIFFUSION POLICY (check quarterly):
1) SIGNATURE AND CONTENT OF THE TWO PERPRES.
> The binary event.
> Then read for three things specifically: (a) any NUMERIC adoption target, (b) any SANCTION, (c) a named implementing agency with a budget line.
> A Perpres with none of these is a press release.
2) THE FIRST IMPLEMENTING REGULATION.
> AI content labelling/watermarking is stated to be first — its issuance date and whether it carries penalties is the test of whether the framework has teeth (China's equivalent took effect 1 Sept 2025).
3) BUDGET LINE ITEMS.
> Look for AI diffusion spending in the APBN and in Komdigi/Kemenko Perekonomian allocations, and for any actual capitalisation of the Sovereign AI Fund under Danantara (proposed 2027-2029).
> Money is the difference between Stranas KA and AI+.
4) EMERGENCE OF SECTORAL ACTION PLANS.
> Watch for ministry-level 'AI+' analogues from Kemenperin (manufacturing), Kemenkes (health), Kementan (agriculture), Kemendikdasmen (education) and OJK (finance).
> China's plan only became real when MIIT, MOFCOM and MOE issued theirs in 2026.
5) DEMAND-SIDE SUBSIDY INSTRUMENTS.
> Any Indonesian compute voucher, model voucher, UMKM AI subsidy, or tax incentive for AI adoption would be the strongest single signal of genuine policy transfer.
6) A NATIONAL AI-USAGE STATISTIC.
> If BPS or Komdigi begins publishing a recurring generative-AI penetration series (beyond the annual APJII question), or an enterprise AI-adoption survey, the state is preparing to manage the number.
7) GOVTECH MILESTONE.
> The October 2026 nationwide GovTech launch and the 2026-2029 government AI-adoption schedule — track how many of the 8 'quick win' projects actually ship, especially the MBG free-meals monitoring system.
8) SAHABAT-AI TRACTION.
> Downloads, MAU, government-service integration, and whether any ministry adopts it as default.
> A domestic assistant reaching even 10 million MAU would materially change the consumer penetration curve.
9) CHINA-CHANNEL ACTIVITY.
> WAICO working groups Indonesia joins; Chinese standards or evaluation frameworks referenced in Indonesian regulation; the Tsinghua branch campus; new Alibaba Cloud/Huawei/Tencent enterprise wins; Chinese compute investment.
10) COMPUTE ENERGISED, NOT ANNOUNCED.
> MW actually live versus the ~580 MW base and 1.3 GW pipeline; availability of frontier models in an Indonesian region.
11) EDUCATION SIGNAL.
> Whether Coding & AI moves from OPTIONAL to COMPULSORY in the school curriculum, and the count of new AI/data prodi approvals — China's mandatory 'AI+ Education' build-out to 2030 is the comparator.
12) PROCUREMENT LANGUAGE.
> Appearance of AI requirements in LKPP/government tender specifications and in BUMN procurement — the quiet mechanism by which state demand creates a domestic market.
13) SEARCH AND MARKET SIGNALS.
> Google Trends Indonesia for 'AI agent', 'DeepSeek', 'Qwen', 'Sahabat AI'; job postings for AI engineers and AI governance roles; DJKI trademark and OSS business-permit filings containing AI terms.

### Hambatan & Faktor Pembatal

**Hambatan Transfer**

> 1) LEGISLATIVE AND ADMINISTRATIVE INERTIA.
> The AI Perpres has missed at least three announced deadlines (early 2026, H1 2026, still pending in August 2026).
> Indonesia's pattern of passing headline instruments and then stalling on implementing regulations and supervisory institutions (UU PDP is the template) is the single largest brake.
2) NO CASCADE MECHANISM.
> Even a signed Perpres cannot assign adoption targets to autonomous regional governments or to private firms.
> Indonesia's decentralised system has no analogue to China's provincial performance evaluation.
3) FISCAL CONSTRAINT AND CROWD-OUT.
> The ~US$15 billion free nutritious meals programme and other priority spending leave little room for compute vouchers or adoption subsidies; the Sovereign AI Fund is deferred to 2027-2029 and unfunded.
4) TALENT SHORTFALL OF 400,000-500,000 PER YEAR.
> A diffusion mandate needs people to configure, integrate, evaluate and govern deployments.
> Indonesia cannot staff one.
5) COMPUTE AND POWER.
> 580 MW of capacity, grid reliability issues outside Java-Bali, and dollar-denominated GPU costs against a rupiah-denominated budget.
6) LANGUAGE AND DATA THINNESS.
> Bahasa Indonesia is under-represented in frontier training data and regional languages far more so; government and sectoral data is largely un-digitised or siloed, so agents have little to act on.
7) LOW DIGITAL LITERACY DESPITE HIGH CONNECTIVITY.
> 81.8% of Indonesian internet users have never used AI — a literacy and relevance gap, not an access gap.
8) FRAGMENTED INSTITUTIONAL OWNERSHIP.
> Komdigi, Kemenko Perekonomian, BRIN, Kemendikdasmen, Kemenperin, OJK and Danantara all hold pieces; reporting describes ministries continuing separate initiatives while the unified roadmap is repeatedly delayed.
> No single accountable owner.
9) GEOPOLITICAL BALANCING.
> Indonesia must run a dual stack — US hyperscaler infrastructure with Chinese open-weight models — while avoiding dependence on either bloc.
> WAICO membership alongside Nvidia/Microsoft/Cisco partnerships is a deliberate hedge, but hedging slows decisive commitment.
10) MSME STRUCTURE.
> Roughly 65 million MSMEs, mostly micro and informal, with no IT function, no digitised process, and no capacity to absorb an adoption mandate.
11) TRUST AND GOVERNANCE UNCERTAINTY.
> Unclear liability rules, incomplete UU PDP enforcement, and a reportedly sanction-light draft framework leave regulated sectors (banking, health) cautious about autonomous deployment.

**Faktor Pembatal Transfer**

> STRUCTURAL REASONS THE CHINESE MODEL WILL NOT ARRIVE IN INDONESIA IN THE SAME FORM — regardless of political will:

1) THE TARGET-CASCADE IS A PROPERTY OF THE CHINESE STATE, NOT OF AI POLICY.
> '70% by 2027' is enforceable because the Party can make it a cadre evaluation criterion for provinces, a KPI for SASAC-supervised SOEs, and a condition of ministerial performance.
> Indonesia's post-1998 decentralised, coalition-governed, electorally accountable system has no equivalent transmission belt.
> An Indonesian president can sign a target; he cannot make 38 provinces and hundreds of thousands of firms hit it.
> This is not a capacity gap that closes with time — it is a different constitution.

2) NO STATE-OWNED INDUSTRIAL VANGUARD OF COMPARABLE WEIGHT.
> China's diffusion runs first through central SOEs in energy, telecoms, heavy industry and transport that can be ordered to deploy.
> Indonesian BUMN are fewer, financially strained, and currently being consolidated under Danantara for value recovery rather than tasked as technology adopters.

3) THE ECONOMY BEING DIFFUSED INTO IS DIFFERENT.
> China is applying AI to the world's largest manufacturing base (over 30% of above-scale manufacturers already adopting) and a vast formal service sector.
> Indonesia's economy is ~57-58% informal, commodity- and consumption-heavy, with a thin advanced-manufacturing layer.
> 'AI+ Manufacturing' with 1,000 industrial agents and 100 manufacturing datasets has no Indonesian counterpart to plug into.
> The high-value diffusion targets simply do not exist in the same density.

4) NO DOMESTIC MODEL INDUSTRY TO CAPTURE THE VALUE.
> China's 1.2-trillion-yuan core AI industry and 6,600 AI companies mean state-driven demand recycles into domestic capability and jobs.
> Indonesian adoption sends value to US and Chinese vendors.
> A Chinese-style diffusion push in Indonesia would function as an import-stimulus programme — which is precisely why the political case for one is weak.

5) COMPUTE SOVEREIGNTY IS UNREACHABLE AT NATIONAL SCALE.
> 1.59 million PFLOPS versus ~580 MW of general data-centre capacity is not a gap Indonesia closes; it is a gap Indonesia routes around by consuming foreign inference.
> Any 90%-penetration target would depend on foreign compute, which contradicts the sovereignty framing the policy is sold on.

6) ARCHIPELAGIC GEOGRAPHY AND ELECTRICITY.
> Uniform national penetration targets are physically implausible where grid reliability, latency and digital literacy vary enormously between Jabodetabek and eastern Indonesia.
> China's targets assume an integrated national grid and network.

7) MEASUREMENT INFRASTRUCTURE DOES NOT EXIST.
> China governs diffusion partly because CNNIC, QuestMobile and the National Data Bureau make it visible (602 million users, 499 million app MAU, 1.4 trillion tokens/day).
> Indonesia has one annual survey question.
> An unmeasurable target is an unmanageable one, and Indonesian policymakers know it — which is one reason no target has been set.

8) THE HARM-REGULATION HALF ALSO REQUIRES CAPACITY INDONESIA LACKS.
> China's companion-AI rules worked because CAC could compel ByteDance and Alibaba to shut features within weeks.
> Indonesian regulators cannot compel OpenAI, Google or ByteDance at that speed, and blunt instruments (platform blocking) carry costs China does not face.

### Prediksi Timeline di Indonesia

**Tahun Masuk Indonesia**

> PARTIALLY ALREADY ARRIVED, ON TWO DIFFERENT CLOCKS.
> MASS CONSUMER DIFFUSION: arrived 2023-2025 and is compounding — ~42-43 million Indonesians (18.2% of internet users) have used generative AI by 2026, with Indonesia a top-15 global ChatGPT market, entirely without policy.
> STATE DIFFUSION POLICY: entering 2025-2027 — the White Paper landed August 2025, the two Perpres are drafted and awaiting signature (slipping through 2026, realistically signed late 2026 or 2027), the government AI-adoption schedule runs 2026-2029, GovTech launches nationally in October 2026, and the Sovereign AI Fund is slated for 2027-2029.
> Take 2026-2027 as the year Indonesia acquires a formal national AI diffusion framework — but a guidance-and-roadmap framework, not a target-and-subsidy one.

**Skenario Percepatan**

> (1) The two Perpres are signed with a named implementing agency, a budget line, and — decisively — at least one numeric adoption target; (2) a free, genuinely good Bahasa Indonesia assistant reaches mass distribution (Sahabat-AI at scale, or Doubao/Qwen/DeepSeek launching a localised free Indonesian consumer app, which would replicate China's penetration mechanism directly); (3) the Sovereign AI Fund is actually capitalised by Danantara ahead of the 2027-2029 schedule; (4) a visible government win — the MBG free-meals AI monitoring system demonstrably reducing leakage — creating political ownership of AI diffusion; (5) fiscal or revenue pressure making AI-driven state efficiency politically attractive (the GovTech/state-revenue framing already points this way); (6) Chinese vendors subsidising aggressively through WAICO-linked capacity-building, compute donations, or free enterprise tiers, exactly as Chinese platforms subsidised their way into Indonesian e-commerce and payments; (7) compute coming online faster than planned (the 1.3 GW pipeline, Nvidia expansion) collapsing local inference cost; (8) Coding & AI moving from optional to compulsory in the national curriculum; (9) a competitive shock — Vietnam, Malaysia or Thailand announcing a China-style diffusion target and Indonesia responding to avoid falling further behind its 49th Global AI Index ranking.

### Dampak Sosial-Ekonomi

**Dampak Daerah Non Jawa**

> STRUCTURALLY EXCLUSIONARY UNLESS DESIGNED OTHERWISE — and this is where a Chinese-style national target would do the most damage if copied naively.
1) THE PENETRATION GAP IS ALREADY GEOGRAPHIC.
> APJII's 2026 data show Java continuing to dominate internet penetration and usage; AI usage concentrates further because it correlates with English, tertiary education, formal employment and device quality.
> A national average penetration target would be met by Java and mask eastern Indonesia entirely — precisely the failure mode of averaged national targets in an archipelagic state.
2) COMPUTE AND CAPABILITY CLUSTER IN THREE PLACES.
> Data centres, AI factories and talent programmes concentrate in Jabodetabek, Batam and Bali.
> The 580 MW base and 1.3 GW pipeline are not distributed development; they are enclave infrastructure with high capital and low local employment.
3) LANGUAGE IS THE DECISIVE VARIABLE.
> Models perform worst in Javanese, Sundanese, Minang, Bugis, Batak and eastern Indonesian languages — so AI is least useful exactly where development need is highest.
> Sahabat-AI's regional-language coverage is therefore not a nice-to-have; it is the main equity instrument available, and it is the one thing in Indonesian AI policy with no Chinese equivalent problem (China has dialects but a single written standard).
4) THE GENUINE REGIONAL UPSIDE.
> The most promising AI applications for non-Java are agriculture (crop-yield forecasting is already one of the eight quick-win projects), fisheries, disaster early warning, remote health, and distance education — all of which are stronger use cases outside Java than in it.
> A diffusion policy organised around SECTORS rather than average penetration would naturally favour the regions.
5) A DELIBERATE SITING LEVER.
> Data annotation, corpus construction and AI evaluation work is geographically footloose and could be sited in Makassar, Padang, Manado, Malang or Kupang.
> Alibaba Cloud's precedent of running AI training roadshows into Aceh, Padang, Makassar and Papua shows this is feasible when required as a condition.
6) POWER REMAINS THE HARD LIMIT.
> Grid reliability and cost outside Java-Bali cap serious compute decentralisation this decade regardless of policy intent.

### Kaitan Pendidikan

**Jurusan Terancam**

> This item threatens programs less through automation than through IRRELEVANCE TO THE NEW POLICY AND DEPLOYMENT ECONOMY:
1) PURE PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION / ADMINISTRASI NEGARA taught as procedure, filing and manual bureaucratic process — the 2026-2029 government AI-adoption schedule and the GovTech rollout obsolete precisely the routine administrative competencies these programs certify.
> The field survives only if rebuilt around digital government, service design, data governance and algorithmic accountability.
2) ILMU PERPUSTAKAAN, KEARSIPAN, AND MANAJEMEN PERKANTORAN at the manual-processing level.
3) STATISTIK AND MATEMATIKA taught without computation, and INFORMATIKA taught as syntax-level programming without systems, data, ML or deployment content — the diffusion economy needs integrators and evaluators, not coders of the kind AI already replaces.
4) HUKUM taught as document drafting and rote statute recall, without technology law, data protection, or algorithmic accountability — while AI/data governance law becomes one of the fastest-growing legal specialisms globally.
5) ILMU KOMUNIKASI / JURNALISTIK taught as content production rather than verification, provenance and information integrity — AI content labelling regimes (China's since Sept 2025, Indonesia's planned as the first implementing rule) make verification a regulated professional function.
6) SASTRA / BAHASA ASING AND PENERJEMAHAN in their current form — the clearest casualty internationally, and the field China has cut most aggressively.
7) MANAJEMEN and generic BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION without data, AI-tool fluency or process-redesign content — Indonesia's largest enrolment block producing its most generic graduates.
IMPORTANT QUALIFIER: none of these fields should be closed.
> The threat is to the LEVEL and the CURRICULUM, not the domain.
> The Chinese lesson is redesign — keep the discipline, move the human to direction, verification and accountability.

**Jurusan Dibutuhkan**

> POLICY AND GOVERNANCE — the growth area this item creates directly, and the one Indonesia is least prepared for: AI governance, audit and assurance; technology and data-protection law (UU PDP, the incoming Perpres and its derivatives, AI content-labelling compliance); AI ethics and public policy; algorithmic accountability and model-risk management for banks and insurers; AI standards and conformity assessment (China alone is producing >50 national/industry standards by 2026 — every one implies assessors); AI procurement and vendor management for government.

DIGITAL GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC-SECTOR DELIVERY: digital government / GovTech program management; public-sector data governance and interoperability; service design; monitoring-and-evaluation with AI (directly relevant to the eight quick-win projects, from MBG meal monitoring to Koperasi Merah Putih financial tracking).

DEPLOYMENT ENGINEERING, NOT MODEL RESEARCH — the highest-leverage technical category for an AI-importing country: data engineering and pipeline construction (the true binding constraint in Indonesian organisations); MLOps and model operations; AI agent orchestration and systems integration; AI evaluation, benchmarking and quality assurance; retrieval and knowledge-system engineering for Indonesian legal, tax, health and agricultural domains; cybersecurity for AI systems.

LANGUAGE AND DATA SOVEREIGNTY — Indonesia's unique defensible niche: computational linguistics for Bahasa Indonesia and regional languages; corpus construction and curation; low-resource-language NLP; AI evaluation for Indonesian cultural and religious context (including syariah-relevant evaluation).
> This is where Sahabat-AI must be staffed from and where no foreign lab has an advantage.

PHYSICAL LAYER: data-centre engineering, power systems, thermal/cooling engineering, electrical contracting — the 1.3 GW pipeline is a real, non-offshorable jobs pipeline.

DOMAIN-PLUS-AI HYBRIDS, mirroring China's 2026 catalogue logic ('AI for business', 'data intelligence'): AI in agriculture and food security, AI in health systems, AI in mining and energy, AI in maritime and logistics, AI in education, AI in public finance and tax administration.

**China Education Response**

> China's education response to AI diffusion is itself a diffusion instrument, and it is far more systematic than anything Indonesia has attempted.
1) 'AI+ EDUCATION' AS A NAMED NATIONAL ACTION PLAN.
> The Ministry of Education announced the AI+ Education action plan on 10 April 2026, building a comprehensive AI education system spanning primary school through university, with full implementation targeted by 2030.
> This makes education one of the six AI+ domains rather than a downstream adaptation.
2) COMPULSORY AI EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS.
> AI instruction has been mandated in primary and secondary education, with Beijing requiring a minimum of eight hours of AI education per academic year for all primary and secondary students from the 2025 autumn semester, and national guidelines pushing AI literacy across the K-12 system.
> Contrast with Indonesia, where Coding and AI is an OPTIONAL subject under Permendikdasmen 13/2025 and explicitly not required of schools lacking facilities.
3) MASSIVE HIGHER-EDUCATION RESTRUCTURING.
> Between 2021 and 2025 Chinese universities ended or suspended roughly 12,200 undergraduate programs and introduced roughly 10,200 new ones, executed through the MOE's annual undergraduate major catalogue rather than left to market attrition.
> AI undergraduate programs went from 35 approved institutions in 2018 to more than 600 universities by 2026.
> The 2026 catalogue added 38 new majors including AI for business, embodied intelligence, brain-computer science, data intelligence, and low-altitude economy management, with nine universities authorised for embodied intelligence and a new 'interdisciplinary studies' category created for fields that no longer fit the old taxonomy.
4) CURRICULAR REDESIGN OVER CLOSURE.
> Communication University of China cut five production-oriented programs while creating 'Intelligent Imaging Art'; a 60-year-old Swahili translation course was redesigned so students learn to DIRECT AND MANAGE AI translators.
> The doctrine is: keep the domain, move the human up to direction, verification and accountability.
5) THE MECHANISM IS THE LESSON.
> This happened at speed because the MOE controls the national major catalogue and enrolment quotas, permitting annual realignment of higher education to industrial policy.
> Indonesia's Kemendiktisaintek has a weaker version of the same instrument through prodi accreditation and quota approval, and does not currently use it strategically.
6) WHAT CHINA IS PLAUSIBLY GETTING WRONG: the scale and speed of humanities and foreign-language elimination, and the risk that 600+ AI programs produce a glut of mediocre AI graduates.
> Indonesia should copy the MECHANISM and the DIRECT-THE-AI curricular philosophy without the scale of humanities destruction.

### Pelajaran Kebijakan dari China

**Respons Kebijakan China**

> THE CRITICAL OBSERVATION FOR THIS ITEM: China did NOT wait for diffusion to mature before regulating harms.
> It runs adoption promotion and harm regulation on parallel tracks, with different agencies owning each.
> That sequencing is the single most transferable insight.

WHAT CHINA HAS ENACTED, IN ORDER:
1) Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (2023) — licensing/filing, content obligations, security assessment.
> Established that a provider must be identifiable and accountable BEFORE mass deployment.
2) AI-generated content labelling measures, effective 1 September 2025 — mandatory explicit and implicit labelling of synthetic content, with platform-level duties.
> Issued at the same moment as the AI+ Opinions: promote adoption and require provenance simultaneously.
3) The AI+ Opinions themselves (26-27 Aug 2025) embed safeguards inside the diffusion mandate — instructing officials to strengthen employment-risk assessment for AI applications and to steer innovation resources toward job-creating directions, with an 'AI + Employment' framework (tax incentives, reskilling, wage subsidies) under discussion.
4) Judicial doctrine on AI-driven dismissal (2025, published as a model case) — adopting AI is not by itself lawful grounds for termination.
5) Interim Measures for the Administration of AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services — issued 10 April 2026 by CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR, effective 15 July 2026.
> Bans virtual companion and virtual family-member services for minors; requires guardian consent for under-14 users; mandates anti-addiction measures, usage and spending limits, content standards, safety assessments, and heightened protection for elderly users.
> Crucially it EXEMPTS customer service, Q&A, work assistants, education and research — regulating emotional dependence without touching productivity diffusion.
> Enforcement was real and fast: Doubao and Qwen shut down personalised companion agents.
6) AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 and a standards programme targeting >50 national/industry AI standards by 2026 — governance delivered through technical standards rather than only through prohibitions.

WHAT INDONESIA SHOULD ADOPT PREEMPTIVELY, IN PRIORITY ORDER: (i) AI-generated content labelling with actual sanctions — already identified as Indonesia's first implementing rule, so the fastest win available; (ii) minors' protection for anthropomorphic/companion AI, BEFORE mass adoption rather than after, since Indonesia's under-18 online population is enormous and the harm arrives with the app not with the policy; (iii) provider accountability and filing for large-scale public-facing AI services; (iv) mandatory employment-impact assessment attached to large-scale public-sector AI deployment; (v) governance through standards and conformity assessment (BSN/SNI) rather than only through a Perpres, because standards scale where enforcement capacity does not; (vi) publish diffusion metrics — a national generative-AI penetration series and public-sector AI deployment register — because China's ability to govern diffusion rests on measuring it.

**Rekomendasi Kebijakan Indonesia**

> 1) SIGN THE PERPRES — AND MAKE IT NON-EMPTY.
> Three tests: a named implementing agency with budget authority, at least one enforceable obligation with a sanction, and a mandatory reporting/measurement mechanism.
> A guidance-only Perpres after three missed deadlines would confirm Stranas KA's failure mode rather than correct it.
2) DO NOT COPY THE 70%/90% TARGET.
> Indonesia cannot cascade, subsidise or measure it, and an unmeetable target destroys policy credibility.
> Set instead SECTOR- AND SERVICE-LEVEL targets that the state actually controls: e.g.
> all national public services with AI-assisted first-line response by 2029; AI-based leakage monitoring live in MBG and Koperasi Merah Putih by 2027; a fixed number of ministries with published AI deployment registers.
> Target what you own.
3) SUBSIDISE DEMAND, NOT JUST SUPPLY — the most copyable Chinese instrument.
> Compute and model vouchers for UMKM and mid-market firms, funded modestly (even a fraction of Shanghai's ~1.4 billion CNY scale would be transformative in Indonesia), delivered through existing MSME channels.
> This moves adoption faster per rupiah than research grants, and it builds a domestic integrator industry.
4) FUND THE LANGUAGE LAYER AS PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE.
> Bahasa Indonesia and regional-language corpora, evaluation benchmarks, and domain datasets (health, legal, tax, agriculture) should be state-funded open goods.
> This is the highest-return, lowest-cost sovereignty investment available and the only one where Indonesia has an absolute advantage.
> Sahabat-AI should be the vehicle, with sustained funding rather than sponsorship.
5) BUILD MEASUREMENT BEFORE MANDATES.
> Commission BPS and Komdigi to publish a recurring national generative-AI adoption series (population, enterprise, by province and sector) and require public bodies to register AI deployments.
> China governs diffusion because CNNIC, QuestMobile and the National Data Bureau make it visible; Indonesia currently has one annual survey question.
6) REGULATE HARMS ON A PARALLEL TRACK, STARTING NOW.
> Issue the AI content-labelling rule with sanctions; adopt minors' protections for companion/anthropomorphic AI ahead of mass adoption (China's 15 July 2026 measures are a ready template); and require human review plus named accountability for automated decisions in public services, credit and employment.
> None of this slows adoption — China proves it.
7) TIE INCENTIVES TO LOCAL CAPABILITY.
> Condition data-centre incentives, government AI procurement and any Sovereign AI Fund disbursement on local hiring, skills transfer, local-language capability and domestic integrator participation.
> Otherwise a diffusion push is an import-stimulus programme.
8) CAPITALISE THE SOVEREIGN AI FUND EARLIER AND NARROWER.
> 2027-2029 is late.
> A smaller fund deployed in 2026-2027 into corpora, public-sector pilots and shared compute for universities and MSMEs would do more than a large fund arriving after the adoption curve has been set by foreign vendors.
9) MAKE CODING AND AI COMPULSORY, WITH TEACHER CAPACITY FIRST.
> The current optional status guarantees the Java/non-Java gap widens.
> China mandated it; Indonesia has 97% teacher training participation to build on.
> Sequence: teacher capacity and devices, then compulsion, with an explicit non-Java rollout schedule.
10) USE WAICO STRATEGICALLY, NOT PASSIVELY.
> Founding membership is leverage: negotiate for compute access, standards co-development, corpus/tooling transfer and training places, rather than accepting standards adoption as a courtesy.
> Simultaneously maintain the US-stack hedge — the dual-stack posture (US infrastructure, Chinese open models) is Indonesia's strongest bargaining position and should be made explicit policy.
11) GIVE ONE INSTITUTION CLEAR OWNERSHIP.
> Fragmentation across Komdigi, Kemenko Perekonomian, BRIN, Danantara and sectoral ministries is repeatedly cited as why the roadmap keeps slipping.
> Name a single accountable coordinator with convening power over sectoral plans.

### Peluang & Rekomendasi Aksi

**Peluang Bisnis**

> 1) AI GOVERNANCE, AUDIT AND COMPLIANCE SERVICES — a market created by regulation, currently near-zero in Indonesia.
> The Perpres, its three-tier risk classification, mandatory content labelling, risk reporting duties (biometrics, IP, deepfakes) and sectoral derivatives from OJK and Kemenkes will generate demand for assessment, documentation, watermark verification and assurance.
> First movers with credible methodology will define the market.
2) PUBLIC-SECTOR AI SYSTEM INTEGRATION — the 2026-2029 government adoption schedule, the October 2026 GovTech launch and the eight quick-win projects (MBG monitoring across 83 million beneficiaries, crop-yield forecasting, Koperasi Merah Putih financial tracking) represent a large, budgeted, addressable pipeline for local integrators who understand both government procurement and AI deployment.
3) BAHASA INDONESIA AND REGIONAL-LANGUAGE DATA SERVICES — corpus construction, annotation, evaluation, red-teaming, and domain datasets for Indonesian legal, tax, health, halal and syariah contexts.
> Labour-intensive, cost-advantaged, sitable outside Java, and the one layer of the stack where foreign labs cannot outcompete Indonesians.
> Exportable to global labs that need Indonesian coverage.
4) VERTICAL AI AGENTS FOR UMKM AT INDONESIAN PRICE POINTS — the Chinese lesson is that free or near-free consumer-grade tooling drives penetration.
> Whoever productises WhatsApp-native vertical agents (klinik, distributor, ekspedisi, sekolah, koperasi, warung) at sub-Rp500k/month captures a 65-million-MSME base that no foreign vendor is serving.
5) DEPLOYING CHINESE OPEN-WEIGHT MODELS AS A SERVICE — DeepSeek, Qwen and GLM can be self-hosted for regulated Indonesian clients (banks, government, health) that cannot send data offshore.
> Sovereign/on-premise inference is a defensible local business precisely because the models are free and the deployment is not.
6) COMPUTE AND DATA-CENTRE ADJACENT SERVICES — with ~580 MW installed and 1.3 GW sought, cooling, power engineering, electrical contracting, colocation operations and specialised staffing are physical, local and non-offshorable.
7) AI LITERACY AND CERTIFICATION AT NATIONAL SCALE — 81.8% of Indonesian internet users have never used AI, and the AI Centre of Excellence targets 1 million trained by 2027 against a 9-million-by-2030 talent requirement.
> Training tied to employer hiring commitments is a durable business.
8) MEASUREMENT AND MARKET INTELLIGENCE — Indonesia has no QuestMobile or CNNIC equivalent for AI.
> A credible recurring Indonesian AI adoption index would be bought by vendors, investors and government alike.
9) CONTENT PROVENANCE AND WATERMARKING TOOLING — if labelling becomes the first implementing rule, every platform, broadcaster, agency and publisher in Indonesia needs compliance tooling.
10) EDGE AND LOW-CONNECTIVITY AI FOR NON-JAVA — offline-capable, low-bandwidth AI for agriculture, fisheries, health outposts and schools in regions the mainstream stack ignores.

**Rekomendasi Individu Mahasiswa**

> 1) SPECIALISE IN THE GAP BETWEEN POLICY AND DEPLOYMENT.
> The scarce Indonesian profile is not 'AI engineer' and not 'policy analyst' — it is someone who can read a regulation and build or audit a compliant system.
> AI governance, audit, evaluation and standards work is a career that barely exists in Indonesia today and will be in structural shortage the moment the Perpres is signed.
2) LEARN DEPLOYMENT, NOT MODEL RESEARCH.
> Indonesia will import models and build integrations.
> Data engineering, retrieval systems, agent orchestration, evaluation and MLOps are where the durable, well-paid, non-automatable Indonesian jobs are.
3) WORK ON INDONESIAN-LANGUAGE AI.
> Contributing to Sahabat-AI, regional-language corpora, Indonesian evaluation benchmarks, or domain datasets builds a credential no foreign competitor can match and sits at the centre of national policy priority.
4) UNDERSTAND GOVERNMENT AS A CLIENT.
> The 2026-2029 public-sector adoption schedule, GovTech, and the eight quick-win projects make government the largest single AI buyer in Indonesia this decade.
> Learning public procurement, e-government architecture and programme monitoring is unglamorous and highly employable.
5) READ THE ACTUAL POLICY DOCUMENTS — the State Council AI+ Opinions, China's sectoral action plans, Indonesia's AI White Paper and draft Perpres, and the EU AI Act.
> Almost nobody in the Indonesian job market has, and comparative policy literacy is a genuine differentiator in consulting, law, government and corporate strategy.
6) BUILD BILINGUAL/TRILINGUAL CAPABILITY INCLUDING MANDARIN.
> With WAICO membership, Chinese vendors, open-weight Chinese models and a proposed Tsinghua campus, the ability to work directly with Chinese technical and policy material is a rare and rising asset.
7) TREAT FREE CHINESE OPEN MODELS AS YOUR PERSONAL INFRASTRUCTURE.
> DeepSeek, Qwen and their derivatives give an Indonesian student the same model capability as a Silicon Valley startup at zero cost.
> The constraint is skill in using and deploying them, not access.
8) GET PROOF OF WORK, NOT JUST CREDENTIALS — shipped projects, open-source contributions to Indonesian-language AI, and public writing.
> In a market with no established AI-governance profession, visible work IS the credential.

**Rekomendasi Perguruan Tinggi**

> OPEN OR EXPAND: AI Governance, Audit and Technology Law (as a genuine interdisciplinary program, not an elective) — the single largest unmet demand this policy creates; Digital Government / GovTech and public-sector data governance (aligned to the 2026-2029 adoption schedule); Data Engineering and MLOps as a track distinct from Data Science; AI Evaluation and Assurance; Computational Linguistics for Bahasa Indonesia and regional languages; Data Centre and Power Systems Engineering; and applied domain-plus-AI hybrids explicitly modelled on China's 2026 catalogue logic (AI for agriculture and food security, AI in health systems, AI in public finance, AI in maritime and logistics).

REDESIGN RATHER THAN CLOSE: Administrasi Negara around digital government, service design and algorithmic accountability; Hukum around technology, data-protection and AI liability law; Ilmu Komunikasi around verification, provenance and information integrity (a regulated function once content labelling is mandatory); Statistika and Informatika around computation, systems and deployment; Sastra and Penerjemahan around directing and auditing AI language systems — the Chinese Swahili-course model.

INSTITUTIONAL ACTIONS: (1) Make AI literacy a compulsory general-education course for every prodi — the highest-return single intervention, and the direct analogue of China's mandatory K-12 AI education.
> (2) Establish AI policy and governance research centres capable of independently evaluating the Perpres and its implementing rules; Indonesia currently has almost no domestic capacity to critique its own AI policy.
> (3) Create a national program-realignment cycle at Kemendiktisaintek modelled on China's MOE catalogue mechanism — evidence-driven, annual, with a deliberate bias toward curricular conversion over closure.
> (4) Partner with government on the eight quick-win projects as live capstone environments, so students graduate having built real public-sector AI systems.
> (5) Use WAICO and bilateral channels to secure faculty exchange, joint labs and training places rather than only vendor certification pipelines — and negotiate for capability transfer, not branded courseware.
> (6) Site AI programs, annotation training and compute access deliberately outside Java, or the national capability map will simply reproduce the existing penetration map.

### Faktor Risiko & Sisi Gelap

**Dampak Negatif China**

> 1) TARGET-DRIVEN FORMALISM AND WASTED CAPITAL.
