> Numeric penetration targets assigned to provinces and SOEs create strong incentives to report adoption rather than achieve it — 'AI face projects' (面子工程), demonstration scenarios with no production use, and duplicated local compute centres built for target compliance rather than demand.
> The pre-existing evidence is stark: only 4.5% of surveyed SOE executives in 2022 said internal digital transformation was meeting expectations and 60% were at an early stage, yet these same firms are the mandated adoption vanguard.
> Mandating AI adoption onto un-digitised processes automates dysfunction.
2) EMPLOYMENT DISPLACEMENT AS THE POLICY'S OWN CENTRAL RISK.
> Youth unemployment reached 18.9% in August 2025 and was still 16.9% in March 2026, with employment sentiment at record lows in central bank surveys, and the state's own planners now debating universal basic income and subsidising low-productivity jobs.
> The diffusion push runs directly against the regime's performance-legitimacy dependence on employment.
3) HARM AT CONSUMER SCALE ARRIVING BEFORE THE GUARDRAILS.
> Emotional dependence on companion AI reached a scale that required five agencies to intervene, forcing Doubao and Qwen to shut down personalised companion features used by very large numbers of people in July 2026 — with millions losing accumulated chat histories overnight.
> The regulation was necessary; the fact that it was necessary is the damage report.
4) MINORS AND ELDERLY EXPOSURE.
> The 2026 companion measures exist because minors were forming relationships with AI systems at scale and elderly users were exposed to manipulation and spending harms.
5) INFORMATION-ENVIRONMENT DEGRADATION.
> Content labelling became mandatory in September 2025 because synthetic content, deepfakes and AI-generated misinformation had already saturated Chinese platforms.
6) CONCENTRATION AND COMPETITIVE DISTORTION.
> Free consumer tiers funded by platform balance sheets (Doubao at 382m MAU, >1.2 trillion tokens/day) make sustainable independent competition nearly impossible; diffusion succeeds partly by concentrating the market in a few very large firms.
7) MEASUREMENT DISTORTION.
> Once penetration becomes a governed target, the statistics measuring it become politically loaded — a general problem with Chinese target-driven policy that makes independent verification of the 2027 '70%' claim effectively impossible.
8) ENERGY AND RESOURCE COST of a compute build-out sized to a 90%-penetration target.

**Risiko Sosial Indonesia**

> 1) ADOPTION WITHOUT ABSORPTION — the core risk.
> Indonesian society is adopting AI faster than the Indonesian state can direct, measure or regulate it.
> Roughly 42-43 million users already, no signed regulation, no measurement series, no content-labelling rule in force, no minors' protection.
> Every month of delay locks in foreign default platforms and imported norms.
2) HARMS ARRIVE ON THE VENDOR'S SCHEDULE, NOT THE REGULATOR'S.
> China needed five agencies and a hard shutdown to address companion-AI dependence among minors.
> Indonesia has an enormous under-18 online population, weaker parental digital literacy, and no equivalent rule even drafted.
> Deepfake fraud, AI-generated scams, non-consensual imagery, and election manipulation ahead of 2029 are all live and unaddressed.
3) POLICY THEATRE.
> The gravest institutional risk is a Perpres that is signed, celebrated, and toothless — repeating Stranas KA (six years, nothing binding) and Surat Edaran 9/2023 (voluntary, unenforced).
> That outcome would consume the political window while changing nothing.
4) COPYING THE WRONG HALF OF THE CHINESE MODEL.
> Importing adoption ambition (targets, mandates, sovereign funds) without importing the safeguards (labelling, minors' protection, employment-risk assessment, judicial limits on AI-driven dismissal) would produce the worst available combination: accelerated displacement, foreign value capture, and no protection.
5) DIGITAL DIVIDE HARDENING INTO A CAPABILITY DIVIDE.
> 81.8% of internet users have never used AI; Java and Gen Z dominate what usage exists.
> National-average targets would mask and worsen this.
> AI could become the mechanism that converts Indonesia's connectivity success into a new inequality.
6) FISCAL RISK ON THE SOVEREIGN AI FUND.
> State capital deployed at scale into AI infrastructure, managed through Danantara, in a country with weak project-selection track records and thin technical evaluation capacity, is an obvious vector for waste and rent-seeking.
> China's version at least recycles into a domestic industry; Indonesia's may not.
7) DEPENDENCE AND GEOPOLITICAL EXPOSURE.
> Building the national stack on Chinese open-weight models plus US hyperscaler infrastructure is pragmatic but creates two dependency surfaces simultaneously.
> Open weights mitigate lock-in but not the dependence on foreign model roadmaps, safety choices, and embedded values — including on topics where Chinese model behaviour reflects Chinese content rules.
8) PUBLIC-SECTOR AI WITHOUT DUE PROCESS.
> Deploying AI into the MBG programme, cooperative finance tracking and GovTech touches eligibility, benefits and enforcement for tens of millions.
> Without a right to human review, explanation and appeal, errors become injustices at scale — and Indonesia's draft framework is reported to be guidance-oriented.
9) LANGUAGE AND CULTURAL MARGINALISATION of Indonesia's non-Indonesian-speaking populations if the language layer remains unfunded.
10) TALENT DRAIN.
> The small pool capable of building this capacity is exactly the pool most employable abroad and by foreign remote employers.

**Kelompok Rentan**

> 1) THE 81.8% OF INDONESIAN INTERNET USERS WHO HAVE NEVER USED AI — older, less educated, non-English-speaking, and outside Java.
> As services, government interfaces and commerce become AI-mediated, non-users move from 'not benefiting' to 'excluded'.
2) CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS.
> Indonesia has a very large under-18 online population, high social-media use, and no companion-AI or minors' protection rule even drafted, while China needed emergency measures effective July 2026 to address exactly this harm.
> Indonesian minors are currently exposed to a class of harm that a peer state has already judged serious enough to force product shutdowns.
3) NON-JAVA AND RURAL POPULATIONS — worst model performance in their languages, weakest connectivity quality, least compute proximity, and lowest probability of appearing in any national average.
4) SPEAKERS OF REGIONAL LANGUAGES — hundreds of languages with negligible representation in training data; without funded corpora, AI accelerates linguistic marginalisation.
5) CIVIL SERVANTS IN ROUTINE ADMINISTRATIVE ROLES, especially in regional governments, as GovTech and the 2026-2029 adoption schedule automate document processing and first-line service response.
6) BENEFICIARIES OF AI-ADMINISTERED SOCIAL PROGRAMMES — the 83 million people in the free nutritious meals programme and cooperative members subject to AI financial tracking.
> Automated eligibility, attendance or fraud flags without a guaranteed right to human review and appeal turn technical errors into denied benefits.
7) ELDERLY INDONESIANS — targets of AI-enabled fraud, deepfake scams and manipulative interfaces; China explicitly wrote elderly protection into its 2026 companion measures.
8) INFORMAL AND MICRO-ENTERPRISE WORKERS (57-58% of employment) — outside every adoption programme, outside enterprise tooling, and outside the data on which policy is built.
9) WOMEN IN ADMINISTRATIVE AND CLERICAL ROLES — the occupational category most exposed to the diffusion this policy would accelerate.
10) VICTIMS OF SYNTHETIC MEDIA — with no content-labelling rule in force and a 2029 election cycle approaching, targets of deepfake harassment, fraud and political manipulation have no specific legal remedy.

### Contoh Kasus Konkret

**Kasus China**

> CASE 1 — THE STATE COUNCIL 'AI+' OPINIONS, 26-27 AUGUST 2025.
> The first government document anywhere to attach numeric, dated penetration targets to economy-wide AI adoption: >70% penetration of next-generation intelligent terminals and AI agents by 2027, >90% by 2030, a 'fully intelligent economy and society' by 2035, across six named domains (science and technology, industry, consumption, public wellbeing, governance, global cooperation).
> Deliberately modelled on 'Internet+' (2015).
> Its significance is structural: numeric targets can be cascaded to ministries, provinces and SOEs as performance indicators, converting an aspiration into an administrative programme.

CASE 2 — THE SECTORAL CASCADE OF 2026.
> The umbrella plan became real through ministry-level implementation: MIIT with eight agencies on 'AI+ Manufacturing' to 2027 (3-5 general-purpose industrial models, 1,000 industrial intelligent agents, 100 high-quality manufacturing datasets, 500 demonstration scenarios); MOFCOM with seven departments on 'AI+ Consumption' (18 June 2026); MOE on 'AI+ Education' (10 April 2026, full implementation by 2030); MIIT targeting >50 national and industry AI standards by 2026.
> This is the mechanism Indonesia most conspicuously lacks.

CASE 3 — SHANGHAI'S DEMAND-SIDE SUBSIDIES.
> Roughly 900 million CNY for enterprise access to computing clusters, models and training data, plus around 500 million CNY over three to five years for company innovation — one city paying firms to CONSUME AI.
> Compute vouchers and model vouchers are the most transferable instrument in the whole Chinese playbook because they attack the buyer-side cost barrier that actually limits diffusion.

CASE 4 — THE CONSUMER FLYWHEEL.
> CNNIC's 57th report (5 Feb 2026): 602 million generative-AI users, 42.8% of the population, +141.7% year-on-year from 249 million (17.6%) at end-2024.
> QuestMobile: AI-native apps at 499 million MAU by May 2026 (+85.4% YoY), Doubao 382m, Qwen 167m, DeepSeek 130m, with users averaging 92.7 sessions and 183 minutes per month.
> In August 2025 the same series showed Doubao at 157 million and DeepSeek at 143 million — meaning Doubao alone added roughly 225 million MAU in nine months.
> Free pricing plus excellent native-language performance, not policy, is what produced this.

CASE 5 — TOKEN CONSUMPTION AS A GOVERNED METRIC.
> National Data Bureau Director Liu Liehong, China Development Forum, 23 March 2026: daily national token invocation exceeded 1.4 trillion, up from about 100 billion in early 2024 — more than a thousandfold in two years, with Doubao alone above 1.2 trillion tokens/day by April 2026.
> The state publishing a real-time diffusion metric is itself the policy innovation: what is measured can be targeted.

CASE 6 — THE COMPANION-AI SHUTDOWN, 15 JULY 2026.
> Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services (issued 10 April 2026 by CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR) banned virtual companion and virtual family-member services for minors, required guardian consent under 14, and imposed anti-addiction, spending and duration controls — while explicitly exempting customer service, Q&A, work assistants, education and research.
> Doubao and Qwen shut down personalised companion agents.
> This is the cleanest demonstration anywhere that a state can regulate a specific AI harm hard and fast WITHOUT slowing productive diffusion.

CASE 7 — THE SOE CONTRADICTION.
> In 2022, only 4.5% of surveyed SOE executives said internal digital transformation was meeting expectations and 60% described their firms as at an early stage — yet these are the enterprises the state most wants leading AI adoption.
> The gap between mandate and absorptive capacity is the strongest available evidence that penetration targets do not by themselves produce productivity.

**Padanan Indonesia**

> Indonesia has a partial analogue to each Chinese case, all weaker and all later:
- STATE COUNCIL AI+ OPINIONS → the two draft Perpres (National AI Roadmap and AI Ethics/Governance) plus the 179-page White Paper.
> UNSIGNED as of August 2026 after at least three missed deadlines, with no numeric penetration target and reportedly guidance-rather-than-sanction oriented.
> Indonesia's older analogue, Stranas KA 2020-2045, produced no binding regulation in six years.
- SECTORAL CASCADE → does not exist.
> Ministries are described as continuing separate initiatives while the unified roadmap is repeatedly delayed.
> The closest thing is the 2026-2029 government-body adoption schedule in the draft Perpres and the eight 'quick win' projects.
- DEMAND-SIDE SUBSIDIES → none.
> The proposed Sovereign AI Fund under Danantara (>US$900bn AUM) is scheduled for 2027-2029, uncapitalised, and oriented to research, public pilots and infrastructure rather than to firm-level adoption vouchers.
- CONSUMER FLYWHEEL → real but shallower: ~42-43 million users, 18.2% of internet users, ~14.9% of population versus China's 42.8%; Indonesia is a top-15 global ChatGPT market.
> The missing ingredient is a free, excellent, Indonesian-language mass-market assistant — Sahabat-AI (Indosat/GoTo/Nvidia, app released February 2026) is the attempt, at a fraction of Doubao's distribution.
- TOKEN/DIFFUSION METRIC → nothing.
> Indonesia's only recurring national AI-usage number is a single APJII survey question.
> No enterprise adoption series, no public-sector AI register, no compute utilisation figure.
- COMPANION-AI AND CONTENT REGULATION → content labelling is identified as the FIRST implementing rule under the coming Perpres, which would parallel China's September 2025 measures, but nothing is in force and no minors'/companion-AI rule is drafted.
- SOE ADOPTION VANGUARD → GovTech/INA Digital national launch October 2026 with ~80% system connectivity and AI-processed data integration across eight ministries is the nearest equivalent, but it is a government-services programme, not an industrial adoption mandate.
- POLICY-BLOC ALIGNMENT → Indonesia as a FOUNDING MEMBER of WAICO (Shanghai, 17 July 2026) with 28 other economies, signed by Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto — the single strongest institutional link, and the most likely channel for future Chinese-style instruments to arrive.
- EDUCATION CASCADE → Permendikdasmen 13/2025 making Coding and AI an OPTIONAL subject (grades 5, 7, 10 from 2025/2026, not required where facilities are lacking; 97% teacher self-training participation by July 2026) versus China's compulsory K-12 AI education and MOE 'AI+ Education' plan to 2030.

### Tingkat Keyakinan & Kualitas Sumber

**Catatan Kontradiksi Data**

> 1) THE 70%/90% TARGET IS NOT OPERATIONALLY DEFINED.
> Public sources uniformly report 'penetration of new-generation intelligent terminals and AI agent applications' exceeding 70% (2027) and 90% (2030), but no source specifies the denominator — 70% of what? Enterprises? Key-sector firms? Devices shipped? Users? Secondary reporting freely substitutes 'AI adoption across key sectors', which is a materially different claim.
> Treat the numbers as real policy signals whose achievement will be unverifiable externally.
2) INDONESIAN AI ADOPTION FIGURES ARE MUTUALLY IRRECONCILABLE.
> APJII 2026: 18.2% of internet users have used AI.
> Microsoft Work Trend Index 2026: 33% of Indonesian workers are 'Frontier Professionals' (double the global average).
> Vendor material: '92% workplace AI adoption — the world's highest' and '62% of Indonesian companies will adopt AI'.
> These measure different populations (all internet users vs employed workers vs enterprises), different intensities (ever-used vs daily vs implemented), and in the 92% case are almost certainly marketing artefacts.
> The APJII figure is the only nationally representative one and should be preferred; the 92% figure should not be used at all.
3) CHINA'S OWN ADOPTION FIGURES CONFLICT WITH ITS DIGITISATION BASELINE.
> Reported enterprise AI-agent deployment of ~79% sits awkwardly with >30% of above-scale manufacturers adopting AI and with the 2022 SOE finding that only 4.5% considered digital transformation to be meeting expectations.
> 'Deployment' in surveys frequently means any pilot; the production-scale figure (~23%) is far more plausible.
4) DEEPSEEK MAU IS DECLINING WHILE ITS INFLUENCE GROWS.
> DeepSeek fell from 143m MAU (Aug 2025) to 130m (May 2026) even as its open weights became a global default.
> Consumer MAU is therefore a poor proxy for a model's diffusion impact — the research brief's framing of DeepSeek as a mass-consumer phenomenon understates its actual role as infrastructure.
5) TOKEN CONSUMPTION IS BOTH THE BEST AND THE MOST GAMEABLE METRIC.
> 1.4 trillion tokens/day is impressive, but Doubao alone accounts for >1.2 trillion of it and the growth is attributed largely to multimodal VIDEO generation.
> Token volume therefore measures compute intensity of the dominant consumer app more than it measures economy-wide productive diffusion.
6) CHINA'S OPENROUTER 'LEAD' IS A NARROW SAMPLE.
> Claims that Chinese models surpassed US models globally rest on OpenRouter share, which captures a small, developer-skewed slice of world inference and excludes first-party OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Azure traffic.
7) INDONESIAN ECONOMIC PROJECTIONS DIVERGE WIDELY: 12% of GDP / US$366bn by 2030 (draft Perpres) versus a 3.67% GDP uplift (separate government-cited estimate) versus a US$10.9bn Indonesian AI market by 2030.
> These cannot all be right; the 12%/US$366bn figure in particular appears to be an economy-wide impact estimate being cited as if it were a policy target.
8) THE PERPRES TIMELINE HAS SLIPPED REPEATEDLY: announced for early 2026, then H1 2026, then 'soon' after clearing harmonisation; reported at various times as sitting with the Ministry of Law and with the State Secretariat.
> Any statement about its status carries a short shelf life.
9) THE ROADMAP PERIOD IS REPORTED INCONSISTENTLY as 2026-2029 and 2026-2030 across outlets, which matters because it determines whether the plan aligns with the presidential term (2029) or with the China/global 2030 horizon.
10) CHINA'S POSTURE IS INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY BY DESIGN.
> The same state that mandates 90% AI penetration by 2030 forced its two largest AI apps to shut down popular features in July 2026 and had courts rule that AI adoption is not lawful grounds for dismissal.
> Both are genuine policy; treating either in isolation misrepresents the model.
11) A DEFINITIONAL CAUTION ON THE RESEARCH BRIEF ITSELF: DeepSeek at 143m and Doubao at 157m MAU are correct for August 2025, but by May 2026 the ranking and magnitudes had changed substantially (Doubao 382m, Qwen 167m, DeepSeek 130m).
> Any analysis anchored on the August 2025 snapshot is nine months stale and understates both the pace of diffusion and Alibaba's rise.
